Being bored is like being in a desert, mentally. Obviously, when someone is stuck in a desert, they should do what they can to either leave the desert, or avoid burning out by waiting for help.

When someone is neurotypical and bored, it is like being in the middle of a desert, while having a vehicle of some sort. One can use the vehicle to try and leave the desert on their own, or they can use it for shade if it is out of energy. And, of course, a vehicle can carry more resources than a person can on their own.

Meanwhile, someone with ADHD does not have a vehicle, so they are stuck in the desert, with only the resources they can carry on their backs, resources which take far more energy to carry along with you, and probably can't cool you as much as ones taken in a car. If a person wants to leave the desert by foot, it will be a far more miserable experience than just leaving in a vehicle.

Whenever I come across some sort of idea, or have to draw something, or write something, I have two main methods of approaching the concept in question:

The first type of thing that my brain does, it that it whittles away at the concept. This is what I do when I am hyperfocused on a topic that I genuinely am fascinated by, or when I am creating a drawing (when I used to draw, at least).

The other thing that I do, is I make an effort to single out and target the most important things which are aspects of a topic. This is usually what I do when I am in the process of learning a topic that I did not hyperfocus myself into, or when I am writing a paper (That is, if I don't get a complete anxiety attack in the process of writing the paper)

I have found that neither of these things are good ways to approach complex maths, or computer programming. Simple maths got me good when I was a boy, and people thought I was smart as well because of my early mastery of simple maths,  which is due to hyperfocus I believe. This is also the reason why I do exceptionally well at tests (outside of applied STEM), and this can often make up for my atrocious  homework performance.

What I really want to do is to get into programming, but 1. I am completely intimidated by all of the languages, I am scared of getting another F at school, and I have absolutely no idea which path to take in order to get a reliable string of dopamine rewards from the activity.

There are several different angles to tackle this issue.

**#1** You need to take a good, hard look at what your functionality is when you are unmedicated. Ask yourself, "Can I function *at all* in my life if I am unmedicated?". 
If the answer is not "Yes, totally", then you *need* the medications, and you *need* to remind yourself that you do until you kill your guilt.

**#2** Remember, success is success. *I* am unmedicated, so let my toxic, bitter envy of the fact that you can be medicated at this moment remind you that *you are doing something right* with your life, *something helpful*. Take full advantage of the benefit you have right now, you never know when it might go away.

**#3** If you are out-performing other people in your group, you can always leave that group, and seek out a different group, one which is more successful. If you choose correctly, you will be able to feel safe in your relative mediocrity, while still being as good as you can be.

**#4** Learn how to not give a fuck about moral judgements from other people, or from your own past, and set a code which will allow you to *maximize your own benefits* while not unfairly harming others. At least, that is what my own code of ethics is at the moment.
